subject: Identifying a constant that may be dropped for sampling

messages.author: 33d5534e21fbbe0f
messages.subject: Identifying a constant that may be dropped for sampling
parts:
Hi, The following statement in the manual defines a parameter, transformed parameter or local model variable as not constant - and therefore required - for updating the sampling joint log-probability.  

"The second difference is that if lambda is not a parameter, transformed parameter, or local model variable, the sampling statement is clever enough to drop the log(lambda) term."

I sometimes get confused as to when something is a constant with respect to updating the sampling log-probability; for example, if i impose a Gaussian prior on a model parameter where the covariance matrix contains no parameters, then it is constant and i can drop the additive logdet term from the log-probability update.  

 however, I'm currently building an lpdf function where it is not clear to me.  I want to update the log-probability for the asymmetric lapace distribution, AL(mu,tau,p) with density function, f(x|mu,tau,p) = tau*p*(1-p)*exp(-tau*rho_{p}(x-mu)),where rho_{p}(u) is the so-called check function.   Here "p" denotes the skewness.  mu, x and tau are parameters.  Suppose I bring "p" into the model in the data block.  Then will the log(p) + log(1-p) terms drop out as constants?

Thanks for your insights.

Terrance.

--
Thank you, Terrance Savitsky

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Identifying a constant that may be dropped for sampling
parts: Missed this the first time around.

> On Oct 5, 2016, at 6:40 PM, terrance savitsky <tds...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi, The following statement in the manual defines a parameter, transformed parameter or local model variable as not constant - and therefore required - for updating the sampling joint log-probability.

Right. Those will all be of type stan::math::var (an autodiff variable)
instead of double in the C++ code. We drop the double arguments using
some template traits programming in C++ at compile time.

> "The second difference is that if lambda is not a parameter, transformed parameter, or local model variable, the sampling statement is clever enough to drop the log(lambda) term."
>
> I sometimes get confused as to when something is a constant with respect to updating the sampling log-probability;

It's exactly as defined. It's not about literally being constant,
it's about where it's defined. If I do this:

transformed parameter {
real a;
a = 4;
}

then Stan can't tell that a is a constant and will not be able to
drop terms involving a from the log density. If a value really is
constant, it should be defined as a transformed data variable and reused.

> for example, if i impose a Gaussian prior on a model parameter where the covariance matrix contains no parameters, then it is constant and i can drop the additive logdet term from the log-probability update.

If that covariance matrix is defined as a data or transformed data
variable or an expression that produces such, then it'll be dropped.
> however, I'm currently building an lpdf function where it is not clear to me.

Nothing gets dropped from user-defined functions. We don't have
a way to inject the relevant C++ traits code.

> I want to update the log-probability for the asymmetric lapace distribution, AL(mu,tau,p) with density function, f(x|mu,tau,p) = tau*p*(1-p)*exp(-tau*rho_{p}(x-mu)),where rho_{p}(u) is the so-called check function. Here "p" denotes the skewness. mu, x and tau are parameters. Suppose I bring "p" into the model in the data block. Then will the log(p) + log(1-p) terms drop out as constants?

Not automatically. But you can drop them yourself manually.

Stan (and most MCMC and optimization routines) only require the log
density up to an additive constant.

- Bob
